postTitle: How Much Insurance Do You Need as Your Wealth Grows?
topic: A covered claim above the policy limit leaves a gap

assumptions.notes: Lesson example: a €500,000 judgment against a €300,000 liability limit leaves €200,000 uninsured.

hookVariants.narration: You owe five hundred thousand euros. Will your insurance pay it all?

Depending on local rules, that gap may come from your savings or income.

cta.subtext: Covered can still leave a gap

caption.instagram:
You owe €500,000 for injuring someone. Will your insurance pay it all?

The example: the policy covers the claim, but the most it pays is €300,000. The remaining €200,000 is uninsured, and depending on local rules it may be pursued from savings or income.

This kind of cover is called liability insurance: it pays what you owe someone else, such as a guest hurt in your home or a cyclist you hit. Serious claims are rare, which is why large limits tend to cost little. As savings grow there is more that a claim above the limit could reach, so the limit is one of the things people look at again.
